question.text: Bluestone Private Credit Fund (Cat II AIF) is about to distribute INR 10 crore of interest income to Helios Partners LP, a Singapore tax resident with valid TRC and Form 10F. ITA rate on interest to non-resident is 20% (Section 115A). India-Singapore DTAA interest article caps at 15%. Under Section 194LBB(b) read with Section 90(2), what is the TDS? (Ignore surcharge/cess.)

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 194LBB(b) prescribes TDS at 'rates in force' or DTAA rate, whichever is MORE BENEFICIAL under Section 90(2). ITA Section 115A: 20% gross. DTAA: 15% gross. 15% is more beneficial for the NR. TDS = 15% x 10 cr = INR 1.5 cr. TRC + Form 10F are preconditions to claim DTAA. The Trap: Option A ignores the DTAA. Option C uses the resident rate. Option D wrongly assumes exemption — DTAAs allocate taxing rights, do not typically exempt interest in the source state. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A treats DTAA at concept level; XIX-C expects CA-supervised TRC validation before applying lower rate. Manager's Pro-Tip: Maintain a 'beneficial-ownership' file per NR LP — India follows substance-over-form. Treaty benefit can be denied on PPT/MLI grounds if the LP is a mere conduit. Collect board minutes, employee count, P&L of the feeder.
